ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening must be run against the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit watchlists, the UN Consolidated List, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list and sectoral sanctions lists, and New Zealand's autonomous sanctions regimes, including the Russia Sanctions Act 2022, before any person is accepted as a shareholder, director, officer, UBO, or authorised signatory. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for all politically exposed persons, as defined in the AML/CFT Act 2009, including foreign, domestic, and international PEPs, their relatives, and close associates. All screening hits must be escalated to the designated compliance officer, and records must be kept for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office online register and name request service (https://companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be in English or te reo Māori. Non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into Latin characters. New Zealand does not impose a four-tier naming convention; the Registrar applies a distinctiveness test requiring a unique first element, an optional descriptive element, and the mandatory legal suffix 'Limited' or its approved abbreviations 'Ltd', 'Co', or 'Company'. The name must not be misleading, offensive, or falsely imply official status.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Companies Office rejects a name, the applicant must file a formal review request within 10 working days through the Companies Office portal or by email to the Registrar, attaching a written submission explaining why the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to a registered name. The submission should cite the Companies Act 1993, the Registrar's naming guidelines, and any prior mark or evidence of distinctiveness. Should the internal review fail, the applicant may seek judicial review in the High Court of New Zealand, with legal representation on record.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: In New Zealand, a registered office must be a physical street address, not a P.O. Box. A virtual office or commercial services address may technically satisfy the Companies Office, but for this ISIC 7320 consumer polling platform the Inland Revenue Department and transactional banks will likely reject a virtual-office-only address because they require evidence of local management, operational substance, or identifiable physical infrastructure. The company must therefore maintain a qualifying physical presence or a contractual suite that includes normal business hours document receipt, director access, and compliance records; a bare mailbox is unacceptable for GST registration and corporate bank account opening.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: maintain complete share register, board minutes, resolutions, key UBO records, financial statements, and service agreements at the registered office; ensure a natural person attends document service during business hours. Quantified risk: approximately 15% over the first two years for a compliant virtual-office SaaS platform; 35-45% if the registered office is a low-cost mail drop, no independent director, or there are unusual associated-party transactions. The Companies Office and IRD may inspect without prior notice.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993, ss 12-20 (Incorporation), s 26 (Constitution), ss 153-160 (Board Resolutions), ss 189-191 (Registered Office), ss 94-97 (Share Allotment), plus Financial Reporting Act 2013 and Companies (Registration) Regulations 1994
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), operating the New Zealand Companies Register
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 - Application for Registration of a Company and Form 2 - Consent to Act as Director, lodged electronically via the Companies Register online portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement under the Companies Act 1993. Shares may be issued unpaid, partly paid, or fully paid at nominal value; no escrow account or capital deposit rule applies to an ordinary New Zealand limited liability company
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED (the Company), passed by unanimous written resolution pursuant to section 160 of the Companies Act 1993 on [Date]. WHEREAS the Company was incorporated with NZBN [Number]. RESOLVED THAT: 1. Share Capital Subscription: the allotment and issue of 100 fully paid ordinary shares of NZD 1.00 each to the founding subscriber be and is hereby ratified and confirmed, with no consideration outstanding and no prospectus requirements applicable. 2. Registered Office: the registered office of the Company shall be situated at [Street Address, City, New Zealand], open to the public during ordinary business hours, and the Registrar of Companies shall be notified of any change of address within 10 working days. 3. Officer Appointments: [Name] be and is hereby appointed sole Director; [Name] be and is hereby appointed Chief Executive Officer; [Name] be and is hereby appointed Chief Financial Officer; each to hold office per the Constitution and the Companies Act 1993. 4. Banking and Payment Rails: the directors be and are hereby authorised to open bank, merchant, PayPal and Wise accounts for the receipt of survey and market research revenues. Dated this [Day] day of [Month], [Year]. Signed: ____________________ (Director).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Availability Search and NZBN Pre-Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office via the Companies Register online portal (companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz) and the NZBN Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a prior name search to confirm the proposed corporate name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name, does not imply Crown patronage or connection with a government body, and is not offensive. Reserve the approved name instantly via the online system and secure the provisional New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) reference. Verify director eligibility, confirming each natural-person director is at least 18 years of age and is not disqualified under section 382 of the Companies Act 1993. A corporate director is permitted only if such director is incorporated and maintains a registered office in New Zealand.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and two alternative names in descending order of preference
Full legal name, date of birth, residential address, and address for service of each proposed director
Identification documents of each director for due diligence
Proposed company purpose aligned with ISIC 7320 market research services
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name application is rejected due to identical similarity, offensiveness, or Crown patronage connotations, the applicant shall file a fresh application with alternative names or make a written submission to the Registrar seeking reconsideration within 20 working days of rejection, citing any prior written consent from the Crown or existing rights holder as applicable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Constitution and Statutory Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholders and licensed incorporation agent or New Zealand legal counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt a bespoke constitution governing share classes, director powers, shareholder meeting procedures, and indemnity provisions. If no constitution is adopted, the default constitution set out in Schedule 1 of the Companies Act 1993 automatically applies. Prepare and execute Form 2 (Consent to Act as Director) for each director and obtain written shareholder consent to the proposed share allotment and officer appointments. Ensure the constitution does not conflict with the mandatory provisions of the Companies Act 1993.
required_dossiers: Constitution of the company (if adopted)
Form 2 - Consent to Act as Director, executed by each proposed director
Shareholders' written consents and share subscription documents
Certified passport or national identity document of shareholder entities and directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the Companies Office queries the constitutional provisions or consents, the incorporation agent shall revise the constitution or resubmit corrected Form 2 consents within 10 business days, or alternatively proceed with the statutory default constitution to eliminate non-compliant clauses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Lodgment of Form 1 Incorporation Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, via the online Companies Register portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form 1 - Application for Registration of a Company electronically, together with the proposed company name, NZBN reference, constitution (if any), registered office address in New Zealand, principal place of business address, share structure, and officer details. Pay the statutory filing fee of NZD 105.50 by credit card or direct debit. On successful validation by the Registrar, the Certificate of Incorporation is issued automatically and an NZBN is permanently assigned. The company acquires legal personality upon issue of the certificate under section 12 of the Companies Act 1993.
required_dossiers: Form 1 - Application for Registration of a Company (electronic)
Form 2 - Consent to Act as Director for each director
Constitution (if custom constitution adopted)
Registered office address and address for service in New Zealand
Shareholder structure and share allotment schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a query or requisition notice, the applicant shall correct the specified defects within 20 working days, including provision of a valid New Zealand registered office address, valid director consents, or corrected share structure data. Failure to cure results in the application being deemed withdrawn, requiring submission of a new Form 1 with a fresh filing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inland Revenue Tax Registration and GST Election
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) of New Zealand, via the myIR secure online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon incorporation, the Companies Office transmits the company file to the IRD, which issues an IRD number by mail within 5 business days. The company must then complete tax registration in myIR: register for Goods and Services Tax (GST) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 on a compulsory basis if annual taxable supplies exceed NZD 60,000, or elect voluntary GST registration; register for employer PAYE obligations if staff are hired under the Income Tax Act 2007 and KiwiSaver Act 2006; and confirm the standard balance date of 31 March. The ANZSIC business activity classification corresponding to ISIC 7320 shall be recorded as market research and statistical services.
required_dossiers: Company Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN
IRD number confirmation letter
Directors' personal identification and IRD numbers
Expected annual turnover estimates for GST registration
Details of any non-resident shareholders for tax residence determination
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If IRD registration is delayed or queried, the applicant shall resubmit the IRD registration form IR 596 with corrected business activity codes and contact details, or contact the IRD Business Hotline for manual intervention; any late GST registration penalty can be remitted upon demonstration of reasonable cause and voluntary disclosure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Constitution of Corporate Register and Registered Office Compliance Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office in conjunction with the appointed director and entity secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Establish and maintain the statutory company register containing the share register, director register, charges register, and officer service agreements. Verify that the registered office remains open to the public during business hours and that the address for service is staffed in New Zealand. File any particulars omitted at incorporation, such as the ultimate shareholder beneficial ownership details required under the Companies Act 1993 (as amended by the Companies (Disclosure of Ultimate Ownership) Amendment Act 2023), via the online annual return and register maintenance facility.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Share register and allotment records
Director and officer registers
Ultimate shareholder ownership disclosure form
Registered office lease or consent of the occupier
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office issues a compliance notice for defective registers or late disclosure of significant ownership information, the company shall file the corrected register entries and pay any prescribed late filing fee; the director may request an extension or remission of the fee by written declaration of inadvertence and prompt remediation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Banking and Cross-Border Payment Rail Onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed New Zealand banks and authorized non-bank payment providers, including PayPal commercial onboarding and Wise Business
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene a board resolution authorizing the opening of a New Zealand corporate bank account and the activation of PayPal Mass Payout and Wise business payment wallet. Complete the customer due diligence process required under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, providing certified copies of the certificate of incorporation, constitution, beneficial ownership register, and director identification. Demonstrate at arm's-length pricing of payment-processing fees; segregation not required. The target payment rails shall be configured to receive and disburse consumer survey incentives lawfully across jurisdictions.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN
Constitution and board resolution authorizing bank and payment provider accounts
Ultimate beneficial ownership register
Identification and proof of address for all directors and signatories
IRD tax registration confirmation letter
Completed AML/CFT entity declaration forms of the respective bank and payment provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or payment provider requests further due diligence information, the company shall promptly furnish additional beneficial ownership charts, source-of-funds declarations, and service agreements with clients; where an application is rejected on compliance grounds, the company shall approach an alternative registered bank or non-bank provider, and the directors may escalate to the Banking Ombudsman only where unreasonable delay has occurred.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - no industry-specific industrial license applies to ISIC 7320 market research and public opinion polling activities; privacy and direct-marketing oversight is exercised by the New Zealand Office of the Privacy Commissioner and the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment under the Privacy Act 2020 and the Unsolicited Electronic Messages Act 2007
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial operating license or manufacturing permit required; the undertaking operates solely as a digital consumer panel survey platform requiring only the certificate of incorporation, NZBN, and IRD tax registrations

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority of New Zealand (EPA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Category C (Exemption from Full EIA) because the platform is an entirely online, non-industrial SaaS service with zero land disturbance, zero stationary energy combustion, and no physical production facility; no activity triggers Schedule 4 of the Resource Management Act 1991
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable - zero wastewater discharge and zero VOC emissions; the sole operational equipment comprises cloud servers and standard office IT assets, with compliance limited to the Waste Minimisation Act 2008 e-waste obligations and general duty to avoid environmental harm under the Resource Management Act 1991; any incidental hardware disposal shall follow approved recyclers registered with MBIE

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification is not required for a virtual-only platform, but to the extent leased office premises are used, they must comply with the Building Act 2004 and the New Zealand Building Code for means of escape and fire warning systems, inspected by Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) at the discretion of the territorial authority; workplace health and safety clearance is required under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, including an employee hazard register, a documented workplace safety management system, first-aid provisions, and electrical safety inspection of all workstation equipment; no heavy machinery, structural load certificate, or civil defense clearance is required for an office and cloud-based business model.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Inland Revenue Te Tari Taake), the national tax authority of New Zealand; electronic filing and registration portal: myIR (https://www.ird.govt.nz); corporate registry: New Zealand Companies Office (https://www.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A New Zealand limited company is incorporated through the Companies Office, which issues the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN); the IRD automatically allocates a company IRD number upon registration and sends the confirmation to the registered office. A non-resident company (including a foreign parent of NZ Ltd) must submit Form IR595 (Non-Resident Company IRD Number Application) with certified proof of incorporation, director and ultimate beneficial ownership details, and New Zealand contact particulars. GST registration is effected through myIR and must be completed within 21 days of the registered person becoming liable; non-resident suppliers of remote services to New Zealand consumers may use the simplified myIR GST registration channel once the NZD 60,000 threshold is exceeded.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (a standard NZ Ltd is a resident company taxed on worldwide income at the 28% corporate rate; New Zealand has no tax-exempt zones and no general territorial exemption; pass-through treatment is available only by elective Look-Through Company (LTC) status, not by default)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Look-Through Company (LTC) election under Part HB of the Income Tax Act 2007 (available to companies with no more than five shareholders, all of whom are individuals, LTCs, or eligible trustees; income and losses flow through to owners); consolidated group and loss-offset elections under the Income Tax Act 2007; imputation group election for franking of dividends; Qualifying Company election (closed to new companies since 2011, grandfathered for existing electors); Australian resident company election to exclude CFC attribution; hybrid mismatch rules under the Taxation (Neutralising Base Erosion and Profit Shifting) Act 2018 apply automatically without elective check-the-box status, consistent with New Zealand's absence of a US-style check-the-box regime.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 (including the remote-services regime added for cross-border digital supplies)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in any consecutive 12-month period; compulsory registration once the threshold is met or expected to be met; voluntary registration permitted below the threshold; non-resident suppliers of remote services must register if supplies to New Zealand resident consumers exceed NZD 60,000 in a 12-month period
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand does not impose a real-time fiscal clearance, IRD digital stamping, or mandatory B2B e-invoicing regime; participation in the voluntary PEPPOL e-invoicing network has been available since October 2023. GST registration, filing, and payments are administered through myIR on monthly, two-monthly, or six-monthly cycles. GST tax invoices must contain prescribed particulars and be issued within 28 days of the time of supply; no pre-clearance by the tax authority is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods are zero-rated under section 11 of the GST Act when supplied by a registered person to a non-resident for direct export or for removal from New Zealand, provided the goods are physically exported by the supplier within 28 days of the time of supply (extended to 365 days where goods are delivered to an approved storage facility for a non-resident). Services are zero-rated under section 11A when supplied to a non-resident who is outside New Zealand at the time the services are performed and the services are not supplied directly in connection with land or goods located in New Zealand. The consumer-panel survey SaaS platform (market research subscriptions, survey design, data analytics, and panel management delivered online) qualifies for zero-rating on supplies to offshore non-resident clients as remote services; the supplier must retain evidence of export and of the recipient's non-resident status.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration lodged through the New Zealand Trade Single Window
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical removal of goods from New Zealand
Carrier or freight-forwarder certificate of export
Foreign buyer contract and purchase order evidencing a supply to a non-resident
Evidence of non-resident status for zero-rated cross-border services (overseas registered address, foreign business registration, IP address and telecom geolocation records)
Foreign currency payment settlement records (e.g., PayPal Mass Payout, Wise, or SWIFT receipts) evidencing inbound proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The IRD maintains a focused compliance programme on zero-rating substantiation; where export conditions (including the 28-day export rule or the non-resident-recipient rule) are not met or cannot be evidenced, the supply is recharacterised as taxable in New Zealand, triggering a GST reassessment, use-of-money interest, and shortfall penalties: 20% for failure to take reasonable care or for an unacceptable tax position, 40% for gross carelessness, 100% where an unacceptable tax position is taken with a dominant purpose of avoiding tax, and 150% for evasion. Criminal liability may arise under the Tax Administration Act 1994 and the Crimes Act 1961 for deliberate falsification. The standard four-year amendment period is extended to eight years in cases of evasion. New Zealand imposes no explicit statutory 180-day FX repatriation deadline; the 180-day benchmark is the recommended contractual standard for substantiating real offshore sales and as a compliance proxy consistent with the IRD's time-of-supply rules and anti-avoidance scrutiny.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand, with the Financial Markets Authority exercising secondary market conduct oversight; New Zealand maintains a fully liberalized no-exchange-control regime and does not require central bank approval for current or capital account transaction execution.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand has full convertibility on both current and capital account. The New Zealand dollar is freely tradable for residents and non-residents, and there are no foreign exchange surrender requirements, no conversion quotas, and no separate capital controls on direct investment, loan repatriation, dividends, or commercial service payments. Profit remittance is unrestricted under foreign exchange law; the only substantive hurdles are company law solvency requirements for distributions, domestic tax withholding on certain payments, and AML/CFT source-of-funds documentation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory surrender timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts. An entity may retain 100% of export proceeds in foreign currency or convert to New Zealand dollars at its discretion. Export receipts may be held in Foreign Currency Accounts offered by New Zealand registered banks, and such balances are freely remittable for trade settlement or future operating expenses, subject only to standard tax record-keeping obligations.

Operating Account - NZD / Foreign Currency / Capital Contribution Account
Operating Account - NZD / Corporate Multi-Currency / Escrow Account
Operating Account - NZD / Wholesale Settlement / Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium. Offshore digital EMI platforms such as Wise and Airwallex are viable for ancillary payout functions if the provider holds an appropriate New Zealand Financial Service Provider registration and money remittance authorization. A pure offshore EMI without New Zealand registration cannot operate as a primary local settlement or deposit-taking banking rail. Legal constraint: New Zealand AML/CFT Act 2009 requires any money remitter servicing the New Zealand market to be supervised by a designated AML/CFT supervisor. Accordingly, the primary treasury account structure should remain with a Tier 1 New Zealand licensed bank, while fintech rails may be used solely for low-value consumer panel payout disbursements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: New Zealand banks do not universally require physical attendance for corporate account opening; however, the practical standard for a newly incorporated New Zealand entity with non-resident directors is either an in-person interview at a New Zealand branch or a recorded video KYC interview with a bank relationship manager. The company must maintain a valid New Zealand registered office and provide certified identity documents for each director, shareholder, and beneficial owner. Most Tier 1 banks will accept electronic identity verification, passport notarization, and a New Zealand statutory declaration; final onboarding remains conditional on the bank's own AML/CFT due diligence determination.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owners or directors resident in high-risk or sanctioned jurisdictions, creating adverse-media and sanctions screening triggers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled passports, certified proof of residential address, CIP screening clearance letters from regulated foreign banks, a corporate benefit-ownership chart showing the full ownership chain, an anti-corruption and sanctions integrity statement, and written confirmation of no direct or indirect exposure to sanctioned persons.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection routed through cryptocurrency exchanges, third-party payment aggregators, or pooled trader accounts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Comprehensive source-of-funds files including audited bank statements from the remitting party, a signed shareholder capital contribution declaration, the underlying commercial contract establishing proceeds for the market research platform, and a contractual undertaking that no crypto or mixed commercial funds will be used for initial capitalization.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border revenue generation from multiple jurisdictions without clear tax substance or transfer-pricing records.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: New Zealand IRD tax registration certificate, an economic-substance file evidencing physical New Zealand premises, employee records, board minutes, annual financial statements, jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction subscriber contracts, and contemporaneous arm's length transfer-pricing documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PayPal Mass Payout or Wise payout rails creating pooled co-mingled settlement flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: AML/CFT-compliant sub-ledger architecture, separately restricted payout-only accounts, no third-party pass-through arrangements, audited reconciliation reports of all recipient payouts, executed platform program agreements with PayPal and Wise, and a written liquidity-flow policy distinguishing customer funds from corporate operating funds.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound share capital or shareholder loan injections must be transmitted by SWIFT MT103 or equivalent high-value interbank wire to the New Zealand operating account. The payment narrative must designate the purpose as 'EQUITY CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION - NZ LTD' or 'SHAREHOLDER LOAN - NZ LTD', with no mixed trade descriptions. Banks will require the supporting verification bundle including: board resolution approving the share issue; shareholders' resolution; share allotment documentation filed with the New Zealand Companies Office; source-of-funds statements from the investor; a capital account allocation instruction; and, where the remittance currency is not NZD, a dated conversion instruction to the bank treasury desk. No RBNZ approval condition applies.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade and supplier disbursements should be executed via SWIFT MT103 for direct cross-border payment, and Commercial Letters of Credit are permissible for larger goods-based procurement. For operating disbursements in New Zealand dollars, the designated clearing rail is Payments New Zealand's Bulk Electronic Clearing System and ISO 20022 local settlement. For global consumer panel payouts, the compliant rails are PayPal Mass Payout and Wise, funded from a dedicated New Zealand operating account, with each payout governed by execution agreements, recipient verification, sanctions screening, and full audit trail reporting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla deliverable foreign exchange forwards in NZD, USD, AUD, EUR, GBP, JPY, and CNH
Non-deliverable forwards for currencies with settlement restrictions, including offshore RMB and selected emerging-market currencies
Cross-currency interest rate swaps between NZD and major trading currencies
Foreign exchange options for option-premium-controlled hedging of material consumer survey revenue receipts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return to the New Zealand Companies Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies, MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 20 working days after the anniversary date of incorporation each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may trigger a Registrar notice, court-enforced compliance, removal (strike-off) from the New Zealand Companies Register, and criminal fines for directors of up to NZD 10,000

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit required if the company qualifies as large (total assets over NZD 60m, revenue over NZD 30m, or 50 or more full-time employees), is an FMC reporting entity, or shareholders holding at least 5% of issued shares validly request an audit
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must comply with NZ IFRS, NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime, or applicable NZ GAAP as set by the External Reporting Board; small non-reporting entities may prepare internal non-statutory accounts

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not maintain a separate annual UBO filing; the annual return confirms registered shareholders and directors, while AML/CFT beneficial-ownership verification is performed by engaged financial institutions; any share transfer must be entered in the Register of Members within 10 working days

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory flat concession for the market research sector; availability of the 15% Research and Development Tax Incentive; imputation credit system for distributed profits; no subnational corporate income tax.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite (subject to 49% shareholder continuity test or business continuity test; no carry-back)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 – Income Tax Return for Companies; electronically filed through Inland Revenue's myIR secure portal; paper filing available but e-filing is mandatory for most registered entities.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 return must be filed by 7 July; for non-standard balance dates, the due date is the 7th day of the fourth month after balance date; tax-agent extensions may apply; provisional tax instalments for March balance date entities fall on 28 August, 15 January and 7 May.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income from sales, services or business activity; for a consumer panel survey platform, this includes all New Zealand-source subscription, data licensing and survey service revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident company without a New Zealand fixed establishment should not include foreign revenue; report only New Zealand-source income connected with a permanent establishment; if no permanent establishment, enter nil and attach explanatory notes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Other assessable income, including interest, dividends, royalties and fees not shown in Box A1.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) exempt or treaty-protected income sourced in New Zealand; disclose any gross amounts where NRWT was withheld at source and claim treaty relief in reconciliation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible business expenses attributable to the New Zealand operation, including salaries, cloud platform costs, third-party survey panel costs, marketing and research expenditures.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses must be incurred in deriving assessable income attributable to the New Zealand permanent establishment; non-resident head-office charges are deductible only at arm's length and with contemporaneous documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income or net loss after allowable deductions and loss offsets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident company with a New Zealand permanent establishment, enter the treaty-compliant attributable profit; for a non-resident with no permanent establishment, enter nil unless filing to claim a loss or a refund of withholding tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carryforward information and continuity of ownership declaration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses carried forward against New Zealand income are available only if the 49% shareholder continuity test is satisfied; substantial non-resident ownership changes may extinguish loss offsets unless the business continuity test is met.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of NZD 50 per month or part-month, capped at NZD 250; late payment penalty of 1% immediately, 4% after seven days, and 1% per month thereafter; Inland Revenue also charges use-of-money interest on unpaid tax at the prescribed rate.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) on gross dividends paid to non-residents, subject to reduction under an applicable New Zealand tax treaty, commonly 15% or 5% for substantial shareholdings.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident beneficial owner must obtain a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its country of residence, provide it to the New Zealand withholding agent before the payment date, and confirm that it has no New Zealand permanent establishment and is the economic owner of the shares; the reduced treaty rate is applied at source; retrospective refund of excess NRWT withheld may be claimed from Inland Revenue within the four-year time bar subject to treaty entitlement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory NRWT on royalties: 15%; statutory NRWT on interest: 15%; typical treaty rates are 10% for royalties and 10% for interest; registered financial institutions may use the 2% Approved Issuer Levy on interest in lieu of NRWT where the borrower is registered and conditions are met; software and data-licence payments may be treated as royalties if the payment is for the right to exploit intellectual property.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NZD 5,000,000 in aggregate annual cross-border related-party transactions; a comprehensive Master File and Local File are administratively expected where cross-border connected transactions exceed this threshold or the multinational group has annual global revenue of at least NZD 50,000,000 and significant New Zealand connected-party activity.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not have standalone Economic Substance Regulations; however, the General Anti-Avoidance Rule in section BG1 of the Income Tax Act 2007 and associated business-purpose doctrines require real economic substance, including local board decision-making, physical governance, employees and operational capability in New Zealand; a mere registered shell company used to access treaty benefits or shift profits will be recharacterised and exposed to shortfall penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately suppressing New Zealand-source revenue, fabricating deductible expenses, maintaining undisclosed foreign bank accounts, or falsely claiming non-residence by using a sham foreign intermediary for consumer survey receipts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under the Tax Administration Act 1994, with imprisonment of up to five years and corporate fines of up to NZD 500,000; civil shortfall penalties up to 200% of the evaded tax; use-of-money interest on all unpaid amounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who directed or knowingly facilitated the evasion are personally liable for the unpaid tax and penalties; courts may impose travel bans, asset restraint orders, disqualification from managing companies and imprisonment upon conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Registering a New Zealand limited company without premises, employees, board activities or commercial substance solely to obtain New Zealand treaty benefits, hold intangible survey technology, or route international payments for tax avoidance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Application of the General Anti-Avoidance Rule to cancel the tax advantage; recharacterisation of transactions; shortfall penalties of up to 100% of the resulting tax shortfall for an abusive tax position; disclosure of an unacceptable tax position under the mandatory disclosure regime.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally assessed for shortfall penalties if they signed or participated in the avoidance arrangement; continued deliberate conduct can lead to criminal tax evasion charges, travel restrictions and personal restitution orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to implement an AML/CFT compliance programme, conduct customer due diligence, or monitor mass-payout rails such as PayPal and Wise where the platform is obliged under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporate fines of up to NZD 2 million per breach; public warnings and infringement notices; suspension or restriction of payment processing; criminal liability for serious or repeat non-compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers and directors who knowingly allow an AML/CFT breach are personally liable to prosecution with imprisonment of up to two years, disqualification as directors, and confiscation orders; travel bans may be imposed during active criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, interest or royalties to non-residents without deducting the required NRWT, or filing false NRWT exemption certificates to avoid deduction at source.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Immediate assessment of unpaid NRWT; late payment penalties of up to 1% plus 4% and 1% per month; shortfall penalties of up to 200% where the failure is intentional; imprisonment of up to five years for evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for the unremitted withholding tax under statutory director liability rules; they may face personal recovery actions, prohibition from leaving New Zealand while tax debts remain, and criminal sanctions if the failure is wilful.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation, or pricing cross-border related-party platform subscriptions, royalty payments, panel data licensing or management fees at non-arm's-length levels below NZD 5,000,000 aggregate threshold expectations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary transfer pricing adjustment to the arm's-length amount; secondary adjustment and recharacterisation; shortfall penalties of 20% for lack of reasonable care, 40% for an unacceptable tax position, or 100%-200% where abusive or evasive; use-of-money interest on all shortfalls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held jointly and severally liable for shortfall penalties where they cause or assent to the incorrect pricing; in aggravated cases, criminal prosecution, travel bans and imprisonment may apply.
